svg.title: Figure 5. Combined loads on a tube (Beer §8.3, preview of Lab 8)
svg.desc: Three parts. (a) Side view of a tube fixed to a wall at the left. A lever arm at the free end points toward the viewer, and a downward force F at its tip bends and twists the tube. A section is cut a distance L b from the lever; point H is at the top of that section. (b, left) The section seen end-on, with H at the top and K at the side, on the neutral axis. (b, right) Two square stress elements on the tube surface. At H there is a normal stress from bending, M c over I, along the tube, plus a shearing stress from torsion, T c over J. At K the bending stress is zero and only the axial stress P over A remains, while the shearing stress is the torsional stress plus or minus the transverse-shear stress V Q over I t.
